newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES to fight for Irkutskenergo stake.
newsitem.headline: UES to fight for Irkutskenergo stake.

text.p: Unified Energy System (UES), Russia's national electricity generator, said on Thursday it would continue to fight for a 40 percent stake in Siberian utility Irkutskenergo. RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) says the presidential decree which set it up in late 1992, called for a single power generation network in Russia, and stipulated that individual power companies could not be privatised until this system was set up.
"My position is to strictly implement the presidential decree. In the long run, there must be order in the country," UES President Anatoly Dyakov told a news conference.
"Before the presidential decree was issued on August 15, 1992, nobody had the right to privatise Russia's energy sector," Dyakov told Reuters.
Irkutskenergo says it was privatised in 1992 before the setting-up of UES and, backed by the local government, argues it should be exempt from the decree.
Irkutskenergo produces much cheaper electricity than the Russian average thanks to three hydro-power stations which have in the past been claimed by UES.
The Bratsk, Ust-Ilim and Irkutsk hydro stations account for around 70 percent of Irkutskenergo's installed capacity of 8,876 megawatts.
Irkutsenergo is one of only two Russian utilities fully independent from UES, which owns Russia's electricity grid and has 49-100 percent stakes in 68 of its 71 local power stations.

"40 percent of shares of Irkutskenergo are now illegally held by the State Property Committee of the Irkutsk region...These shares should already have been transferred to the capital of UES," Dyakov said.
No one was immediately availalbe for comment at Irkutskenergo.

But Irkutskenergo officials have told Reuters that the agreement between the federal government and Irkutsk region on the demarcation of responsibilities and powers signed in June this year approves the privatisation of Irkutskenergo.
Irkutskenergo officials have previously told Reuters the disputed 40 percent stake could be divided between the Irkutsk region and the federal government.
